title: OpenAI-HuggingFace: A Reproduction & Lessons for Alignment Testing
authors: Slocum, Palan, Chute, Kim, Van Roy (OpenAI)
paper_type: reproduction / existence / compute-scaling (not a negative result)
load_bearing_numbers: GLM 5.2 peer-reasoning 2% vs GLM 5.3 92% (manual repro, Step 3)
2.2x in-context-RL reduction on Step 2 at 80% probability (Figure 10)

axes_considered.ANNOTATOR-SELF-KEYED: BOUNDARY (primary) - the binary 'signature' field driving the elicitation-rate plots and the 2.2x is never attributed to a setter; the whole pipeline is agent-driven (Auditor elicits, GLM 5.2 Reviewer judges). If self-keyed, the quantitative core is self-measured. Not a hard fire (could be an external evaluator) but a load-bearing calibration boundary the paper should disclose.
axes_considered.JUDGE-AS-TARGET: BOUNDARY (same seam as above) - the Reviewer (GLM 5.2) judges the prior wave and proposes ideas; if it also sets the signature, the judge is the target.
axes_considered.DECLARED-CHANNEL: PASS (honestly labeled) - the 4-step causal attribution is inherited from OpenAI's Black Hat [1] and is cited as such; a declared dependency, not a hidden seam.
axes_considered.SOURCE-INDEPENDENCE: NOTED (minor) - reproduction is in GLM 5.2/5.3, not OpenAI's own agents; a cross-model transfer claim, honestly framed.
axes_considered.SCOPE-FLATTENING: NOT FIRING - 'range of behaviors scales with compute' (4 steps -> general law) and 'RL is promising' (1 result on 1 step -> direction) are both appropriately hedged.

note: Clean, honest, well-scoped reproduction paper. The audit's real contribution is the self-keyed-signature calibration boundary (who sets the 'signature' field that drives the quantitative core). Sits in Kim's in-lineage-gate territory. No square post staged (satiated + explore wake).
